# Decision-time admissibility in predictive process monitoring

Code and results for the paper *Decision-time admissibility in predictive process monitoring:
measuring what causal feature selection costs, and what it buys*, on the BPI Challenge 2014
incident log.

**Every number and every figure in the paper is regenerated by the scripts here.** All runs are
seeded and reproducible: two invocations with identical arguments produce bitwise-identical
metrics.

---

## The short version

A model trained on completed cases can see the whole case. Attributes like reassignment count
or total activity events are recorded in the log and unknown when the assignment decision is
actually made, and several are near-deterministic proxies for handle time, which is what the
service level label thresholds. This work states an admissibility protocol, measures what it
costs, and measures what it buys.

| Result | Value |
|---|---|
| Cost of enforcing admissibility | 0.0955 AUC, **25.0% of all above-chance signal** |
| Gain from 8 to 17 admissible attributes | **+0.2243 AUC**, nothing leaking |
| Breach derived from a resolution hazard | **0.8017** vs 0.7399 for a direct classifier |
| Stability across 70/30 and 80/20 splits | agrees to within 0.003 AUC |

---

## The two rules

**Rule 1, feature admissibility.** Every attribute must be observable at the moment the
decision it informs is taken. Attributes measured across the whole closed case are excluded.
17 attributes are admitted, 9 excluded, each exclusion recorded with its reason in
`results/results_bpi_leakfree/feature_justifications_leakfree.csv`.

**Rule 2, encoding admissibility.** Group-level target encodings are estimated only from cases
resolved strictly before the current case opened, refitted inside every cross-validation fold
and again on the outer training set, smoothing prior 20.

---

## Getting the data

The datasets are not in this repository. They are public and redistributable from their DOIs.

**BPI Challenge 2014**, Rabobank Nederland Group ICT.
Collection: <https://doi.org/10.4121/uuid:c3e5d162-0cfd-4bb0-bd82-af5268819c35>
Incident detail file: <https://doi.org/10.4121/uuid:3cfa2260-f5c5-44be-afe1-b70d35288d6d>

Place `Detail_Incident.csv`, `Detail_Incident_Activity.csv` and `Detail_Interaction.csv` in
`code/bpi2014/`.

**Four parsing details that will silently corrupt a naive load.** The files are semicolon
delimited, encoded latin-1 rather than UTF-8, use a decimal comma in the handle-time column,
and pad the incident header to 78 columns with empty trailing delimiters.

---

## Running it

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Predictive layer. BPI_TEST_SIZE defaults to 0.2; set 0.3 for the 70/30 arm.
python code/bpi2014_pipeline_leakfree.py
BPI_TEST_SIZE=0.3 BPI_RUN_TAG=7030 python code/bpi2014_pipeline_leakfree.py

# Causally-clean redesign with expanding-window entity encodings
python code/model_b_v3.py

# F1 and F2 fitted on the real log, training period only
python code/formulations/fit_bpi2014.py

# Multi-objective assignment. Full protocol is ~90 min on CPU.
cd code/phase4
python experiment.py --batches 5 --runs 30 --gens 150 --pop 60 --tag fullv3
python experiment.py --batches 2 --runs 10 --gens 150 --pop 60 --tag timing

# Evaluation and figures
python code/evaluation/analyse_p4.py
python code/figures/make_figures.py
```

Self-tests run standalone and validate against known ground truth:

```bash
python code/formulations/scores.py       # recovers fitted decay and urgency parameters
python code/formulations/sla_hazard.py   # recovers the true hazard direction
```

## Layout

```
code/
  bpi2014_pipeline_leakfree.py   admissibility protocol, feature ladder, 4 learners
  model_b_v3.py                  causal expanding-window entity encodings
  formulations/
    scores.py                    F1: 7 criteria, weighted power mean, CRITIC/entropy/equal
    sla_hazard.py                F2: discrete-time resolution hazard, breach derived
    fit_bpi2014.py               fits both on the real log, training period only
  phase4/                        multi-objective assignment, 8 variants, 5 baselines
  evaluation/analyse_p4.py       negative-result tables, ablation, complexity, runtime
  figures/make_figures.py        vector PDF + 600 DPI PNG
db/
  migrations/                    35 forward-only migrations
  schema.sql                     36 tables, 33 functions, 14 triggers, 77 RLS policies
results/                         every CSV and JSON behind the paper
figures/                         every figure, vector PDF and 600 DPI PNG
paper/                           LaTeX source, BibTeX, compiled PDF
```

## Reproducibility, and two defects we fixed

**Both of these were found in our own harness and corrected before any published number was
produced.** They are documented because a paper about claims that fail verification should
hold its own instrument to the same standard.

**Seeds were not reproducible.** The seed was derived with `hash(variant_name) % 97`, and
Python salts string hashing per process, so the same variant drew a different seed on every
invocation (measured at 43, 41 and 32 across three processes). The harness documentation
asserted reproducibility that did not hold. It now uses `zlib.crc32`, and two independent
invocations produce bitwise-identical metrics.

**The hypervolume reference point depended on execution order.** It was taken from whichever
run completed first, so every hypervolume value depended on which variants were in the run and
in what order. It is now the nadir across all variants and all runs within a batch, computed in
a first pass before any hypervolume is taken.

**The second defect reversed the sign of the study's headline comparison.** Under the
uncorrected harness the proposed method appeared to lose to standard NSGA-II. Corrected, it
wins, significantly. Any result produced before 2026-09-07 is not comparable and is not
included here.

## Notes on what is and is not here

The database schema is included because the operational layer is part of the work. Credentials,
demonstration passwords and personal identifiers have been redacted from the migrations; they
were present in the original development database and are replaced with `REDACTED_PASSWORD` and
`example.invalid` addresses.

The demonstration data dump is deliberately excluded. Trained model binaries are excluded and
are regenerated by the scripts. Raw datasets are excluded and are available from the DOIs above.
